page.layout: One page of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin (NB. at the top, then a note beside the lines about "Maza"). Running head at top centre, page number at top right, catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: NB. æstate nos magis vesci cibis frigidis & humidis, quod ventriculus sit calidior secundum essentiam primo & per se sed potius ut ventriculus flaccidus, humido scil. in eo per resolutionem & evaporatio-nem tenuium partium absumto, refrigerando & humectando corroboretur, villi resoluti ac relaxati astringantur: his enim laxatis appetitus per-ditur, qui iisdem astrictis restituitur. Cum enim calorem immodicum & redundantem consecuti-ve & necessario comitetur siccitas, quâ in corpore humano nihil periculosius, (ut vidimus in corpo-ribus tabidis & emaciatis, quae sunt sicca absumto videlicet humido radicali) ad hanc præ-canen-dam ventriculum frigido humidis roboramus, cu-jus alias vires prorsus conciderent atq; resoluerentur. Deinde calor æstate sentitur magis in exteri-oribus evocatus scilicet à centro suo ad circum-ferentiam ac per universum corpus dispersus. Atq; hoc est quod Hipp.l.3. de diæt. inquit, cibis mol-lioribus & paucioribus utendum esse ob debilem ventriculi calorem, & maza magis quàm pane, potionibusq; albis, mollibus & aquosis, sc.ad humec-tandum. Consentiunt cum his quæ habentur l. de salubr. diæt. Maza massa farinæ est ex oleo & aqua subacta.Æstate maza molli alioportet & potione aquosa multa, obsonisq; omnibus elixis; & his ita utendum est, ut corpus si frigidum & mol-le. Huc accedit authoritas Celsi, qui inquit, æstate potione & cibo corpus sæpius egere quia videlicet calor externus multum depascitur: calor em ex-ternum nominat & circumfusum non internum, qui

page.notes: The printed text is faded and blotched, especially at the left edge and at the line ends. The word "præcanendam" (split across the line end as "pr- canen-dam") is a conjecture from the broken letters. The phrase "calor em ex-ternum" is unclear: "em" may be a damaged "enim" or "em" abbreviation. The running head reads "PROROGANDA." as printed. The marginal note "Maza massa farinæ est ex oleo & aqua subacta." is placed beside the line "Æstate maza molli" in the right margin. The bottom "G" is the gathering signature and "qui" the catchword. The page is one continuous paragraph with no visible indent, so it is marked as continuing from the previous page.
